panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description:
Amber at 85%, red at 95% (sustained), as VME's Host/VM CPU Usage alarms. Short peaks are normal.

Colors match VME's default HVM alarm thresholds ([HVM alarms](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/alarms.rst)).

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(m.time, $__interval), s.name AS metric, avg(m.value) AS value FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE $__timeFilter(m.time) AND m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) AND (-1 IN ($vm) OR s.id IN ($vm)) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: CPU ready (healthy < 5%, act > 10%)
panels.description:
**CPU ready** is the share of time a VM's vCPUs were ready to run but had to wait for a physical core.
VME reports it per VM as the average across its vCPUs (for a host: across the VMs on it).

| Per vCPU | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **under 5%** | Healthy | Nothing |
| **5 to 10%** | Contention: VMs are queuing for CPU | Check the host's CPU usage and vCPU:core ratio; watch the trend |
| **over 10%** | VMs are noticeably slowed | Move VMs to a quieter host, cut vCPUs on oversized VMs, or add capacity |

Look at sustained values: short spikes during backups, patching or boot storms are normal.
Too many vCPUs per physical core raises ready time for every VM on the host, so right-size large VMs first.

VME added this "CPU Ready-equivalent metric" in 9.1.0; HPE doesn't document how it's calculated or a threshold. At low load it reads several times higher than the kernel's
own measurement (*vCPU wait* on the exporter dashboards), so these thresholds err on the side of warning early.
When the two disagree, trust vCPU wait.

panels.title: Running VMs by peak CPU (idle = never above 5% in 24 hours)
panels.description: Running VMs whose CPU never went above 5% in the last 24 hours (VME's CPU figure, sampled every minute). VME's figure reads about 2% even for an idle VM, so the threshold sits above that. Candidates to power off, shrink or reclaim; check the list on the VME Virtual Machines dashboard first. Change IDLE_PCT / IDLE_WINDOW in tools/build_dashboards.py to redefine idle.

targets.rawSql: WITH w AS (SELECT m.entity_id, max(m.value) AS peak, avg(m.value) AS mean, count(*) AS samples FROM metrics m JOIN servers s ON s.id = m.entity_id WHERE m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric = 'cpu_pct' AND m.time > now() - INTERVAL '24 hours' AND s.present AND s.power_state = 'on' AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) AND (-1 IN ($vm) OR s.id IN ($vm)) GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) >= 10) SELECT s.name AS "VM", h.name AS "Host", s.max_cores AS "vCPU", s.max_memory AS "Memory", w.peak AS "Peak CPU", w.mean AS "Average CPU", w.peak < 5 AS "Idle" FROM w JOIN servers s ON s.id = w.entity_id LEFT JOIN servers h ON h.id = s.host_id ORDER BY w.peak

panels.title: Memory that could be freed
panels.description: Total of the Reclaimable column below. Running VMs: the memory each was given against the most its guest used over the look-back (the **Memory look-back** picker at the top; 30 days by default, so month-end jobs count).

INTERVAL '$mem_window' AND h.bucket < now() - INTERVAL '2 hours' UNION ALL SELECT m.entity_id, m.metric, m.time, m.value FROM metrics m JOIN vm ON vm.id = m.entity_id WHERE m.entity_type = 'vm' AND m.metric IN ('mem_used_bytes', 'mem_guest_used_bytes', 'mem_guest_swap_out_bps') AND m.time >= now() - INTERVAL '2 hours'), u AS (SELECT entity_id, max(value) AS peak, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) AS p95, min(time) AS since, bool_or(metric = 'mem_used_bytes') AS from_api, bool_or(metric = 'mem_guest_used_bytes') AS from_guest FROM samples WHERE metric <> 'mem_guest_swap_out_bps' AND value > 0 GROUP BY 1), sw AS (SELECT entity_id, max(value) AS swap FROM samples WHERE metric = 'mem_guest_swap_out_bps' GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT vm.id, vm.name, vm.host_id, vm.max_memory AS alloc, u.peak, u.p95, u.since, sw.swap, CASE WHEN u.from_api AND u.from_guest THEN 'Morpheus + libvirt' WHEN u.from_api THEN 'Morpheus' WHEN u.from_guest THEN 'libvirt' END AS source, CASE WHEN u.peak IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE greatest(1073741824, ceil(u.peak * 1.25 / 1073741824) * 1073741824) END AS suggested FROM vm LEFT JOIN u ON u.entity_id = vm.id LEFT JOIN sw ON sw.entity_id = vm.id), st AS (SELECT r.*, CASE WHEN r.peak IS NULL THEN 'no guest data' WHEN coalesce(r.swap, 0) > 0 THEN 'swapping: keep' WHEN r.peak >= 0.9 * r.alloc THEN 'tight' WHEN r.since > now() - panels.title: Memory right-sizing (peak used vs allocated, over the memory look-back)
panels.description:
Running VMs: the memory each was given against the most its guest used over the look-back (the **Memory look-back** picker at the top; 30 days by default, so month-end jobs count).

* **Peak used**: the highest reading. **P95**: 95% of hourly peaks were at or below this.
* **Source**: *Morpheus* is the VM memory figure Morpheus reports. *libvirt* is the guest's own figure from the balloon statistics (the libvirt exporter on the HVM host): memory in use without the guest's page cache. With both, the higher one counts.
* **Suggested**: peak + 25%, rounded up to whole GiB, at least 1 GiB.
* **Status**: *can shrink* frees at least 1 GiB and 25% of the VM's memory; *tight* peaked at 90% or more of its memory; *swapping: keep* swapped out inside the guest (libvirt), so it needs what it has or more; *short history* has data for less than 80% of the look-back; *no guest data*: neither source reports the guest's use (see docs/DASHBOARDS.md).

Host-side figures (RSS) are not used: pages a VM has touched stay resident, so they overstate use. Check with the VM's owner before shrinking, and leave room for growth.

targets.rawSql: WITH vm AS (SELECT s.* FROM servers s WHERE s.kind = 'vm' AND s.present AND s.power_state = 'on' AND s.max_memory > 0 AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) AND (-1 IN ($vm) OR s.id IN ($vm))), samples AS ( SELECT h.entity_id, h.metric, h.bucket AS time, h.max AS value FROM metrics_hourly h JOIN vm ON vm.id = h.entity_id WHERE h.entity_type = 'vm' AND h.metric IN ('mem_used_bytes', 'mem_guest_used_bytes', 'mem_guest_swap_out_bps') AND h.bucket > now() - INTERVAL '$mem_window' * 0.8 THEN 'short history' WHEN r.alloc - r.suggested >= greatest(1073741824, 0.25 * r.alloc) THEN 'can shrink' ELSE 'right-sized' END AS status FROM r), c AS (SELECT st.*, CASE WHEN st.status = 'can shrink' THEN st.alloc - SELECT s.name AS "VM", s.power_state AS "Power", s.status AS "Status", h.name AS "Host", cl.name AS "Cluster", s.ip_internal AS "IP", s.max_cores AS "vCPU", s.max_memory AS "Memory", s.max_storage AS "Disk", s.os_name AS "OS", s.guest_agent_status AS "Guest agent", s.agent_version AS "Morpheus agent", cd.name AS "Cloud", s.plan AS "Plan", s.source_image AS "Image", i.owner AS "Owner", s.date_created AS "Created" FROM servers s LEFT JOIN servers h ON h.id = s.host_id LEFT JOIN clusters cl ON cl.id = s.cluster_id LEFT JOIN instances i ON s.id = ANY(i.server_ids) AND i.present LEFT JOIN clouds cd ON cd.id = s.cloud_id WHERE s.kind = 'vm' AND s.present AND (-1 IN ($cluster) OR s.cluster_id IN ($cluster)) AND (-1 IN ($host) OR s.host_id IN ($host)) AND (-1 IN ($vm) OR s.id IN ($vm)) ORDER BY 1
